strongest_objection: VRMSE > 1 ("worse than predicting the mean") is a property of the metric under temporal decorrelation, not a signature of macrostate multiplicity — and this directly contradicts the claim's core exclusion ("NOT turbulence, shocks, or stiffness alone"). Any single-attractor chaotic system with a positive Lyapunov exponent will, once an autoregressive rollout exceeds its predictability (Lyapunov) time, produce pointwise predictions that are effectively independent draws from the same climatology as the target. Two independent draws from one distribution have expected squared error ~2×variance, i.e. VRMSE → √2 > 1, while the constant mean-field predictor scores exactly VRMSE = 1. So ordinary sensitive dependence on initial conditions in a SINGLE macrostate is already sufficient to drive every baseline above 1 at long horizon — no coexisting attractors required. The hypothesis mistakes a generic consequence of chaotic error saturation plus a variance-normalized metric for a specific fingerprint of degeneracy. The evidence is a 2-example confirmatory story (RT, viscoelastic) rather than a test of the biconditional: it never audits the many other VRMSE>1 Well datasets (MHD, turbulent radiative layer, supernova, gravity cooling) that are hard for orthogonal reasons — heavy-tailed dynamic range, sharp fronts meeting spectral-bias architectures — nor does it show that the two cited datasets fail BECAUSE of multistability rather than merely being correlated with it. And "macrostate degeneracy" — coarse-grained states selected discontinuously by unresolvable microstructure — is arguably just spatiotemporal chaos renamed at a coarser scale (RT bubble competition IS chaotic mixing), so the claimed distinction from "chaos alone" may be definitional rather than mechanistic.
prior_art: The Well: a Large-Scale Collection of Diverse Physics Simulations for Machine Learning (Ohana et al., 2024, hf.co/papers/2412.00568) — the source of VRMSE and the rayleigh_taylor / viscoelastic datasets; already reports which datasets exceed VRMSE 1, undercutting novelty of the observation itself

Chaos as an interpretable benchmark for forecasting and data-driven modelling (Gilpin, 2021, hf.co/papers/2110.05266) — establishes Lyapunov-time-bounded predictability and trivial-baseline crossover in chaotic forecasting

Model scale versus domain knowledge in statistical forecasting of chaotic systems (Gilpin, 2023, hf.co/papers/2303.08011) — quantifies predictability horizons in Lyapunov times; error saturation above naive baselines is expected for single-attractor chaos

PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers (Lippe et al., 2023, hf.co/papers/2308.05732) — attributes long-rollout blow-up to neglected frequency/spectral components, a competing mechanism for VRMSE>1

Diagnosing Failure Modes of Neural Operators Across Diverse PDE Families (Shikhman, 2026, hf.co/papers/2601.11428) — offers an alternative failure taxonomy (architecture × PDE family, spectral/rollout diagnostics) that does not invoke macrostate degeneracy

Generalized Teacher Forcing / AL-RNN dynamical-systems-reconstruction work (Durstewitz group, hf.co/papers/2306.04406, 2410.14240) and Chialvo/Rulkov multistability studies (hf.co/papers/2405.05675) — multistability and coexisting attractors are already a studied, named concept in ML dynamics, not a new construct
survives_as: A weaker correlational claim survives: among The Well datasets, physically multistable systems (RT bubble competition, viscoelastic elastoinertial turbulence with coexisting attractors) plausibly sit in the VRMSE>1 group, and physical multistability is a distinct, worth-diagnosing contributor to surrogate failure that is not the same as smoothness/stiffness. Useful as a diagnostic hypothesis — "check whether a hard dataset is multistable" — but NOT as the claimed biconditional fingerprint, and NOT with the exclusion of chaos/turbulence, which is false because Lyapunov decorrelation alone drives the metric past 1.
next_experiment: Take one KNOWN single-attractor, ergodic, non-degenerate turbulent dataset (forced isotropic / Kolmogorov flow, or The Well's turbulent_radiative_layer / MHD) and plot VRMSE versus rollout horizon for the same baselines. If VRMSE crosses 1 purely from temporal decorrelation past the Lyapunov time with a single attractor, the 'NOT chaos alone' claim is falsified outright. Pair this with a specificity/sensitivity audit across ALL Well datasets: correlate VRMSE>1 membership against an independent multistability score (number of coexisting attractors / basin count) AND against a confound proxy (field kurtosis / spectral-slope sharpness). If VRMSE>1 tracks sharpness/heavy-tails better than attractor count, the fingerprint is refuted; if it survives that partialling-out, the reduced claim is supported. Cheap because it reuses existing Well data and pretrained baselines — only inference and metric bookkeeping, no retraining.

strongest_objection: The "novelty" is a renaming of an established evaluation philosophy, and the reframing is strictly less informative than what it replaces. Scoring surrogates by long-term fate rather than short-horizon pointwise error is the core methodology of the dynamical-systems-reconstruction (DSR) field and of chaotic-forecasting benchmarks: Gilpin explicitly argues pointwise/Lyapunov-time error is the wrong yardstick and evaluates via long-horizon statistical/attractor properties; the Durstewitz group's DSR line (Generalized Teacher Forcing, AL-RNNs) scores models by whether they reconstruct the ATTRACTOR — invariant measure, power spectrum, Lyapunov spectrum — not trajectory error; PhyxMamba adds "attractor geometry regularization / dynamical invariants" as its evaluation target. The same idea is standard in ML weather/climate as the "climate vs. weather" distinction (long-run statistics vs. pointwise forecast skill). Turning that continuous invariant-measure comparison into a discrete "which attractor did it land in" CLASSIFIER is a coarse-graining that throws away information: a Brier/continuous invariant-measure score dominates a thresholded macrostate label. Worse, fate-accuracy is a WEAKER discriminator than the paper assumes — a mode-collapsed or over-smoothed surrogate that always relaxes to the dominant basin will score high on fate while being physically useless, the exact failure short-horizon metrics were catching. And the whole framing presupposes viscoelastic_instability is genuinely multistable from a single genesis snapshot (multiple basins reachable under perturbation); The Well's runs vary by parameters, not by basin selection from one initial condition, so "fate" may be degenerate (a constant classifier) — an untested premise, not a demonstrated one.
prior_art: Gilpin, 'Model scale versus domain knowledge in statistical forecasting of chaotic systems' (arXiv 2303.08011) — argues pointwise error is inadequate for chaotic systems; evaluates long-horizon statistical/attractor-level fidelity
Gilpin, 'Chaos as an interpretable benchmark for forecasting and data-driven modelling' (arXiv 2110.05266) — benchmark of chaotic dynamical systems scored on attractor/statistical properties

Hess et al., 'Generalized Teacher Forcing for Learning Chaotic Dynamics' (arXiv 2306.04406) and Brenner et al. AL-RNNs (arXiv 2410.14240) — dynamical systems reconstruction: models judged by attractor reconstruction, invariant measure, Lyapunov/topological properties rather than pointwise error

Liu et al., 'PhyxMamba: Mamba Integrated with Physics Principles ... Long-term Chaotic System Forecasting' (arXiv 2505.23863) — attractor-geometry / dynamical-invariant evaluation of long-term rollouts
PDE-Refiner (arXiv 2308.05732) and JAWS (arXiv 2603.05538) — long-rollout stability is already an explicit, benchmarked evaluation axis for neural PDE surrogates
survives_as: A narrow, incremental empirical contribution: for systems FIRST shown to be genuinely multistable from a fixed genesis snapshot, reporting a basin/macrostate-agreement score over long autoregressive rollouts as a COMPLEMENT to short-horizon VRMSE — and specifically instantiating such a metric on The Well's viscoelastic_instability, which no one appears to have published. This is an application of the existing attractor/invariant-measure evaluation paradigm to one new dataset, not a new benchmarking principle; it must be paired with a degeneracy guard (report fate-classifier base rate and penalize mode collapse) or it can reward smoothed, physically useless surrogates.
next_experiment: Multistability sanity test on the ground truth before building any benchmark: take The Well viscoelastic_instability reference solver, fix one genesis snapshot, run N (~50) rollouts under tiny IID perturbations, and cluster the long-time statistics (e.g. stress/velocity histograms or POD-coefficient distributions). If all N collapse to a single macrostate, 'fate' is a constant label and the whole framing is refuted for this system; if ≥2 stable, well-separated basins appear with a nontrivial split, the fate-classification benchmark is viable and worth building. One solver sweep, no surrogate training needed, decides the premise.

strongest_objection: The claimed novel category — post-hoc, no-retraining conservation enforcement at inference — already exists and is standard: ProbConserv (2023) corrects a black-box surrogate's output to satisfy integral conservation at inference, and ACE/ACE2/CAMulator apply per-step mass/moisture/energy budget corrections at inference to autoregressive emulators, explicitly crediting them for multi-decade stable rollouts. Beyond renaming, the mechanism is underspecified where it departs from that prior art: (a) 'reject' is vacuous for a deterministic surrogate (no alternative step exists, so the gate collapses to projection = prior art); (b) on the specifically named driven-dissipative systems (turbulent_radiative_layer cooling budget) the 'receipt' is a statistical balance with unobservable sub-stride flux terms, not an invariant, so the acceptance tolerance must be tuned — making the gate an ordinary drift clamp confounded with physics-agnostic stabilizers; (c) a global scalar budget constrains ~1 of ~10^5 degrees of freedom, so rollouts can stay 'receipt-valid' while spatially decohering, and if the horizon metric is boundedness rather than fidelity, the claimed extension is circular.
prior_art: Learning Physical Models that Can Respect Conservation Laws (ProbConserv), Hansen et al. 2023 — post-hoc Bayesian enforcement of integral conservation on black-box SciML outputs, no retraining; also shows global-constraint enforcement can hurt pointwise accuracy
ACE: A fast, skillful learned global atmospheric model for climate prediction, Watt-Meyer et al. 2023 — inference-time mass/moisture conservation corrections in a long-rollout autoregressive emulator

ACE2: Accurately learning subseasonal to decadal atmospheric variability and forced responses, 2024 — per-step dry-air-mass and moisture budget correction at inference enabling 80-year stable rollouts
CAMulator: Fast Emulation of the Community Atmosphere Model, 2025 — conserves dry air mass, moisture, and energy for numerically stable climate integrations
ConCerNet (Zhang et al. 2023) — neural projection layer enforcing conserved quantities on dynamical-system predictions
Scaling physics-informed hard constraints with mixture-of-experts, Chalapathi et al. 2024 — differentiable hard-constraint projection for conservation laws
PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers, Lippe et al. 2023 — physics-agnostic long-rollout stabilization baseline the gate must beat
Physics-aware generative models for turbulent fluid flows through energy-consistent stochastic interpolants, Mücke & Sanderse 2025 — energy consistency for stable turbulence rollouts
survives_as: A benchmark/empirical contribution, not a mechanism: on The Well, quantify how much inference-time budget-projection (ProbConserv/ACE2-style) extends fidelity-defined stable horizons (VRMSE/correlation vs ground truth, not mere boundedness) for off-the-shelf pretrained surrogates on driven-dissipative systems whose 'closure' is a source-term budget rather than a strict invariant — a setting prior work did not systematically test — with mandatory ablations against matched physics-agnostic stabilizers. The stochastic-surrogate variant (reject-and-resample among ensemble/diffusion candidates by receipt validity) is the only genuinely under-explored corner of the idea.
next_experiment: Take one pretrained Well checkpoint (e.g., FNO on turbulent_radiative_layer_2D) and roll out under four matched conditions: (a) no gate; (b) receipt-projection gate on the cooling/mass budget; (c) physics-agnostic control of equal correction magnitude (fixed spectral low-pass or per-step norm clamp); (d) placebo gate projecting onto a physically meaningless scalar of similar variance. Report horizon at which correlation with ground truth drops below 0.8. If (b) does not beat (c) and (d), the mechanism is refuted; a boundedness-only 'stability' win with no fidelity win also counts as refutation.
